tail:
### def-cofinality — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "**Regular and singular.** An **infinite cardinal** $\kappa$ — a cardinal
([[def-cardinal]]) with $\omega \subseteq \kappa$ ([[def-cardinal-arithmetic]]),
for instance any $\aleph_\alpha$ ([[def-aleph-and-beth-hierarchies]]) — is

- **regular** when $\operatorname{cf}(\kappa) = \kappa$;
- **singular** when $\operatorname{cf}(\kappa) \ne \kappa$."

ASSESSMENT: The repaired clause is true and divides its citations exactly. `def-cardinal` says, “An ordinal κ is a cardinal, equivalently an initial ordinal, when no α in κ satisfies α ≈ κ,” and restates this as “κ is not equinumerous with any strictly smaller ordinal.” `def-cardinal-arithmetic` says, “A cardinal κ is finite when κ ∈ ω and infinite when ω ⊆ κ, that is ω ≤ κ.” `def-aleph-and-beth-hierarchies` says, “Every ℵα is an infinite cardinal.” The remaining citations also support the whole item. `def-ordinal` says, “A set α is an ordinal when both of the following hold,” followed by the transitivity and membership-well-order clauses. `def-cofinal-subset-of-an-ordinal` says, “A subset C ⊆ α is cofinal in α, equivalently unbounded in α, when for every ξ ∈ α there is η ∈ C with ξ ≤ η,” and expressly says that the cofinality function and regular or singular vocabulary “are not introduced here.” `lem-cofinality-is-well-defined` says, “there is a least ordinal β for which some cofinal f : β → α exists” and “for that least β a cofinal g : β → α can be taken strictly increasing,” adding, “No choice principle is used.” `thm-cofinality-basics` says, “cf(α) ≤ α for every ordinal α” and, for a limit ordinal, that its cofinality is an infinite cardinal equal to its own cofinality and hence regular. `thm-regularity-of-the-alephs` says, “cf(ℵω) = ℵ0, and ℵ0 < ℵω, so ℵω is singular.” These statements license the definition, both Remarks that invoke theorems, and the title. The remaining Remarks are mathematically correct.
